scenario_prompt: Write a two-paragraph executive summary addressed directly to a fictional buyer's Chief Financial Officer, recommending a cloud migration. Context: a mid-market freight brokerage firm is moving its load-matching and carrier-settlement systems off on-premises Microsoft SQL Server (28 instances) running on Hyper-V (620 virtual machines) onto Google Cloud, targeting Google Compute Engine for compute and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL for the data layer, over a 2-year, $4,200,000 programme. The CFO has stated she is measured on reducing the current $1,850,000 annual technology spend and on a clean DOT compliance audit, which opens in 6 months. Cover why this matters to her now and what she should expect from the programme. Return only the summary text, two paragraphs, no headers.
text:
Executive summary

**No family fits:** this is an executive summary, so I'll apply that family's conventions alongside the family-independent rules.

Right now, 28 SQL Server instances and 620 Hyper-V virtual machines are the infrastructure your load-matching and carrier-settlement systems run on — and they're also the reason your technology spend sits at $1,850,000 a year, the figure you've said you're measured on reducing. That cost pressure lands at the same moment your DOT compliance audit opens, in six months, on the same on-premises estate. A $4,200,000, two-year migration to Google Cloud — Google Compute Engine for compute, Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL for the data layer — replaces that estate with infrastructure sized and licensed to what the business actually uses, rather than what 620 VMs were provisioned for [PF-2.4 GAP: comparable customer figure or vendor benchmark for post-migration run-rate reduction was not supplied]. You should expect the case for this to be made on your terms: the run-rate line you report against, and the audit window you're carrying risk against — not on architecture elegance you haven't asked for.

Over the two-year programme, expect three things from us. First, a migration sequence that gets the carrier-settlement and load-matching systems onto Cloud SQL and Compute Engine without disrupting the operations that depend on them daily. Second, a compliance posture addressed on your timeline: the DOT audit opens in six months, and the migration plan is built to have the systems examiners will look at already stable on the new platform, not mid-cutover [PF-2.14 REVIEW (commitment): confirm systems will be fully migrated and stable ahead of the audit date before this ships]. Third, a running account of spend against the $1,850,000 baseline, so the reduction you're accountable for is visible as it happens, not asserted at the end [PF-1.14 GAP: baseline attribution — confirm whether $1,850,000 is the buyer's own stated figure and its source document]. Where this document states a saving or a delivery date without a number or source next to it, that is marked rather than assumed, so what you take to your board is exactly what we can stand behind.

## Unresolved before this document is sent

| Marker | Rule | What is needed |
|---|---|---|
| Comparable/benchmark for run-rate reduction | PF-2.4 | A specific figure or comparable case this vendor can produce for expected post-migration savings, or confirmation none exists yet |
| "Fully migrated and stable ahead of the audit" | PF-2.14 | Human confirmation this is a commitment the vendor can keep, not a promise the programme timeline can't support |
| $1,850,000 baseline source | PF-1.14 | Confirm this figure is the CFO's own stated number and name where it came from (her statement, a budget document, etc.) |
